title: Acids, Bases and pH
summary: Properties of acids and bases, the pH scale and indicators, neutralisation, and the reactions of acids with metals, metal oxides and carbonates.

rows: Vinegar, lemon juice, hydrochloric acid (HCl), sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄)
Baking soda, soap, toothpaste, sodium hydroxide (NaOH)

notes.text: A base that dissolves in water, such as sodium hydroxide.

The **pH scale** runs from **0 to 14** and measures how acidic or basic a solution is. **pH 7 is neutral** (pure water). The lower the pH, the stronger the acid; the higher the pH, the stronger the base.

notes.text: **Indicators** change colour depending on pH. **Universal indicator** shows a range of colours: red (strong acid), orange/yellow (weak acid), green (neutral), blue (weak base) and purple (strong base). Natural indicators can be made from red cabbage or beetroot juice.

notes.title: Naming the salt
notes.problem: Hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide. Name the products.
steps: The salt takes its first name from the metal in the base: sodium.
Its second name comes from the acid: hydrochloric acid → chloride.

items: Indigestion tablets (antacids) neutralise excess stomach acid.
Farmers spread lime (a base) on acidic soil.
Bee stings (acidic) can be treated with baking soda; wasp stings (basic) with vinegar.
Toothpaste neutralises acid made by bacteria on teeth.

rows: acid + metal carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide

notes.title: Acid and a carbonate
notes.problem: Write a word equation for hydrochloric acid reacting with calcium carbonate.
steps: acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide
notes.answer: hydrochloric acid + calcium carbonate → calcium chloride + water + carbon dioxide

notes.label: Safety
notes.text: Always add **acid to water**, never water to concentrated acid, because the heat released can make it spit. Wear safety glasses and rinse any spills with plenty of water.
